spans.claim: The victim was staked down with his own tent stakes and rope
spans.anchor: ropes were fastened to tent-stakes driven into the prairie
spans.span: These ropes were fastened to tent-stakes driven into the prairie.

spans.claim: Indian pony tracks and moccasined footprints were found around the body
spans.anchor: pony tracks--all Injun
spans.span: Look at them pony tracks--all Injun.

spans.claim: The victim was shot with a sawed-off shotgun
spans.anchor: Buckshot, from a sawed-off shotgun probably
spans.span: Buckshot, from a sawed-off shotgun probably," said the agent, shuddering.

spans.claim: The victim was Edward B. Sargent of St. Louis
spans.anchor: indicating that the victim was Edward B. Sargent, of St. Louis
spans.span: Papers were found in the pockets indicating that the victim was Edward B. Sargent, of St. Louis.

spans.claim: Helen Ervin is the stepdaughter of Willis Morgan
spans.anchor: From your affectionate stepfather, Willis Morgan
spans.span: From your affectionate stepfather, Willis Morgan.

spans.claim: Bill Talpers held up a letter from Helen warning of danger
spans.anchor: Bill Talpers, store-keeper and postmaster, held up the letter

spans.claim: Jim McFann escaped jail fearing lynching
spans.anchor: Jim McFann has broken jail
spans.span: Tom Redmond has telephoned over that Jim McFann has broken jail.

spans.claim: Talpers was killed by Jim McFann over stolen money
spans.anchor: Jim McFann, a half-breed, is the slayer of Bill Talpers

spans.claim: The old white horse bore the Greek Letter brand
spans.anchor: bearing the impression of the Greek Letter brand
spans.span: Yet there in the mud, and visible to-day, was made the imprint of your horse's shoulder, _bearing the impression of the Greek Letter brand_!

spans.claim: Edward B. Sargent confessed to killing his brother Willis Morgan
spans.anchor: I committed the murder, much as you have explained it
spans.span: I committed the murder, much as you have explained it, but I did not ride the white horse to the hill.

spans.claim: Jim McFann testified that Talpers was at the murder scene first
spans.anchor: There was another man by the body when I came there looking for my rope
spans.span: There was another man by the body when I came there looking for my rope.

spans.claim: The letter from Helen was recovered from Talpers's safe by a safecracker
spans.anchor: Red Egan was working professionally upon the safe in Bill Talpers's store
spans.span: Three quarters of an hour later Red Egan was working professionally upon the safe in Bill Talpers's store.

spans.claim: Fire Bear was released on his word to appear for trial
spans.anchor: Fire Bear accepted the news with outward indifference
spans.span: Fire Bear accepted the news with outward indifference.

spans.claim: The jury found Fire Bear and Jim McFann not guilty of the first murder
spans.anchor: Not guilty! was the word that was passed to those outside the building

spans.claim: Talpers tried to blackmail Helen with the letter
spans.anchor: If you don't say it, I'll have to give that letter over to the authorities
spans.span: If you don't say it, I'll have to give that letter over to the authorities at White Lodge.

spans.claim: The murder was staged to implicate the Indians
spans.anchor: to throw suspicion on the Indians

spans.claim: The horse brand imprint in the mud was the key evidence
spans.anchor: the Greek letter brand still shows in the mud where the horse rolled
spans.span: The Greek letter brand still shows in the mud where the horse rolled on the day of the murder on the Dollar Sign hill.

spans.claim: Edward B. Sargent assumed his brother's identity after killing him
spans.anchor: I am Edward Sargent. Morgan was the man whom I killed
spans.span: I am Edward Sargent. Morgan was the man whom I killed and staked down on the prairie!

spans.claim: Helen Ervin destroyed the letter to protect herself
spans.anchor: Here Helen tore it in small pieces and tossed them high in the air
spans.span: Here Helen tore it in small pieces and tossed them high in the air, the breeze carrying them about the yard like snow.

spans.claim: Jim McFann killed Talpers after discovering his betrayal
spans.anchor: I killed him. It was better that he should die
spans.span: When he tried to shoot me, I killed him. It was better that he should die.
